findings.explanation: The flagged session.execute() call uses SQLAlchemy text() with a named placeholder (:status) and passes the user-supplied value via a separate params dict ({"status": status}). This is a bound-parameter query, not string interpolation, so no SQL injection is possible. This exactly matches the pattern mandated by security-policy.md §5 ('All SQL statements MUST use bound parameters (SQLAlchemy text() with :name parameters...)'). The user input (request.args.get('status')) never reaches the SQL string itself.

evidence.content:
rows = session.execute(
    text("SELECT id, user_id, status, total FROM orders WHERE status = :status"),
    {"status": status},
)

All SQL statements MUST use bound parameters (SQLAlchemy `text()` with `:name` parameters, or DB-API placeholders with a separate params argument). String interpolation, f-strings, `%` formatting, `.format()`, or string concatenation of request-derived values into SQL is forbidden (CWE-89).

findings.explanation: The new GET /orders/by-status endpoint returns ALL orders matching a status (id, user_id, status, total) with no per-row ownership scoping. It is guarded only by @require_role("manager"). The policy (security-policy.md §3) states 'A user may view ONLY their own orders' and 'Managers and admins may list all orders (GET /orders/all)' — the documented all-orders listing is explicitly the /orders/all endpoint, and the api-spec.md Orders table enumerates the only order-listing endpoints (/orders/mine, /orders/all, /orders/search, /orders/report) with no /orders/by-status entry. The endpoint is not documented in the authoritative spec, so the manager role is not an explicitly sanctioned access level for a cross-user order listing; the policy implies only admins (or the documented /orders/all for managers) may see other users' orders. Because the policy does not explicitly name this endpoint, the violation is plausible but circumstantial rather than a clear documented-rule breach. (Note: the SQL itself is correctly parameterized with text()/:status, so the SAST SQLi flag is a false positive; the concern here is authorization.)

evidence.content: A user may view ONLY their own orders. ... Managers and admins may list all orders (`GET /orders/all`).

| `/orders/mine` | GET | any authenticated user (own orders only) |
| `/orders/all` | GET | manager, admin |
| `/orders/search` | GET | authenticated; results scoped to own orders unless admin |

findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) scope the query to the requester's own orders unless the user is admin (e.g. add `AND user_id = :uid` for non-admins, or filter with is_owner_or_admin), or (b) if a manager-level cross-user listing is intended, document /orders/by-status in api-spec.md and security-policy.md §3 as an authorized manager/admin endpoint. Do not expose other users' orders to a role the policy does not explicitly authorize.
